newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Fiscal deficit is Brazil's top challenge - Cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Fiscal deficit is Brazil's top challenge - Cenbank.

text.p: Brazil's top priority is to cut its fiscal deficit to keep inflation at low levels, said Central Bank International Affairs director Gustavo Franco on Monday.

"The stabilization program is not completed. We will not keep inflation at the low levels we have today for the rest of our lives if the fiscal outlook doesn't improve," said Franco, after addressing a conference on Latin American utilities sponsored by foreign investment bank Caspian Securities.
"The fiscal deficit must be reduced to avoid (high) inflation," he said.
Last year, Brazil showed a nominal deficit of nearly 7.0 percent of Brazil's gross domestic product, Franco said.
Franco said the government aims to "cut the deficit to the lowest possible level" in 1997 but he declined to make any projections.
To help reach this target, Brazil must accelerate its privatizations so as to raise more revenues.
"We have to cut expenses and raise revenues. There is no magic," he said.
